precepts.text: Those "in league" are the peoples in agreement or alliance with Ethiopia, who fall together with Egypt by the sword.
precepts.point: Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, all the mingled people, and the men of the land that is in league shall fall with them by the sword; those that uphold Egypt shall fall and the pride of her power come down.
precepts.why:
“Ethiopia, and Libya, and Lydia, and all the mingled people, and Chub, and the men of the land that is in league, shall fall with them by the sword.” Those “in league” are the peoples in agreement or alliance with Ethiopia. They are joined to Egypt and Ethiopia, so they fall together with them by the sword.

This is the day of the Lord, “a cloudy day; it shall be the time of the heathen.” The sword comes upon Egypt and “great pain shall be in Ethiopia”, and everyone who upholds Egypt falls: “the pride of her power shall come down”. Being in league with her does not save you; it puts you in the same fall, desolate in the midst of the countries that are desolate.

points: Ezekiel is to prophesy, Woe worth the day, for the day of the Lord is near, a cloudy day, the time of the heathen; the sword shall come upon Egypt and great pain in Ethiopia when the slain fall.
Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, all the mingled people, and the men of the land that is in league shall fall with them by the sword; those that uphold Egypt shall fall and the pride of her power come down.

The Most High will make the multitude of Egypt to cease by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and the terrible of the nations, who draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain, drying the rivers and selling the land into the hand of the wicked.

He will destroy the idols, cause the images to cease out of Noph, set fire in Egypt, pour His fury upon Sin, cut off the multitude of No, and send the cities of Egypt into captivity, so they shall know that He is the Lord.
In the eleventh year the word came that the Most High has broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and it shall not be bound up to be healed or made strong to hold the sword.
He will break both Pharaoh's arms, strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put His sword in his hand, scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and they shall know that He is the Lord.
